records.label: Proband (22-month-old female)

phenotypes.text: severe biventricular and biatrial chamber enlargement
normal respiratory chain studies in skin and muscle

records.segregation: de novo; parents unaffected by screening echocardiography
quotes: A 22-month-old female of white European ancestry was diagnosed with fetal cardiomegaly at 30 weeks gestation and delivered one week later for fetal hydrops. Postnatal echocardiography revealed severe biventricular and biatrial chamber enlargement, severe systolic dysfunction (left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 25%; normal >50%), a small apical ventricular septal defect, and a moderate secundum atrial septal defect.
Mild facial dysmorphism (wide-set eyes, down-slanted palpebral fissures, prominent forehead, mild macrocephaly, low-set ears) and bilateral cataracts were also identified.
the resultant c.224C>A, p.S75Y (NM_022157.3) substitution in RRAGC, predicted damaging by SIFT and PolyPhen2, remained as the single most plausible candidate.

records.label: 3 infants with de novo RRAGC missense variants
quotes: Genetic testing via trio exome sequencing was applied to identify the underlying disease cause in 3 infants with dilated cardiomyopathy, hepatopathy, and brain abnormalities, including pachygyria, polymicrogyria, and septo-optic dysplasia.

We identified 3 de novo missense variants in RRAGC (NM_022157.4: c.269C>A, p.(Thr90Asn), c.353C>T, p.(Pro118Leu), and c.343T>C, p.(Trp115Arg)), which were previously reported as occurring somatically in follicular lymphoma.

notes.statement: Reijnders et al. (2023) identified 3 de novo missense variants in RRAGC by trio exome sequencing in 3 infants with dilated cardiomyopathy, hepatopathy, and brain abnormalities; these variants had previously been reported as somatic variants in follicular lymphoma.
quotes: We identified 3 de novo missense variants in RRAGC (NM_022157.4: c.269C>A, p.(Thr90Asn), c.353C>T, p.(Pro118Leu), and c.343T>C, p.(Trp115Arg)), which were previously reported as occurring somatically in follicular lymphoma.

notes.statement: Reijnders et al. (2023) found that patient fibroblasts carrying the T90N variant showed increased cell size, dysregulated p70S6K and TFEB signaling, and mTOR subcellular localization decoupled from metabolic state; key findings were confirmed for all 3 variants in HEK293 cells, consistent with constitutive overactivation of mTORC1.
quotes: Studies of patient-derived fibroblasts carrying the p.(Thr90Asn) variant revealed increased cell size, as well as dysregulation of mTOR-related p70S6K (ribosomal protein S6 kinase 1) and transcription factor EB signaling. Moreover, subcellular localization of mTOR was decoupled from metabolic state.
We confirmed the key findings for all RRAGC variants described in this study in a HEK293 cell model.
The above results are in line with a constitutive overactivation of the mTORC1 pathway.

notes.statement: Reijnders et al. (2023) described de novo missense variants in RRAGC as the cause of an early-onset mTORopathy with unfavorable prognosis.
quotes: Our study establishes de novo missense variants in RRAGC as cause of an early-onset mTORopathy with unfavorable prognosis.

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) noted that, through whole exome sequencing of a pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patient, they had previously identified a de novo S75Y variant in Rag GTPase protein C (RagC, encoded by RRAGC), revealing RRAGC as a new DCM susceptibility gene, but stated that further evidence, including functional studies in animal models and identification of additional RRAGC mutations in DCM cohorts, was required to prove pathogenicity.
quotes: A de novo missense variant in Rag GTPase protein C (RagCS75Y) was recently identified in a syndromic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patient. However, its pathogenicity and the related therapeutic strategy remain unclear.

Through whole exome sequencing of a pediatric DCM patient, we recently identified a de novo S75Y variant in Rag GTPase protein C (RagC, or RRAGC), revealing RRAGC as a new susceptibility gene. However, further evidence is required to prove pathogenicity, including functional studies in animal models and identification of additional RRAGC mutations in DCM cohorts.

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) generated a zebrafish RragcS56Y knock-in line (corresponding to human RagC S75Y) via TALEN technology, targeting the heart-predominant rragca orthologue. Homozygous knock-in fish began to die at 5 months with approximately 70% surviving to 1 year, and exhibited reduced body weight, reduced maximum swimming capacity, decreased ejection fraction and fractional shortening with increased end-systolic volume/body weight ratio, decreased E/A ratio, increased myocardial performance index, enlarged ventricular surface area/body weight, reduced trabecular density, and elevated ventricular myosin heavy chain (vmhc) transcript.
quotes: We generated a zebrafish RragcS56Y (corresponding to human RagCS75Y) knock-in (KI) line via TALEN technology. The KI fish manifested cardiomyopathy-like phenotypes and poor survival.
The rragc KI fish started to die at 5 months, with approximately 70% fish surviving to 1 year of age (Figure 1E).
We noted significant ventricular systolic function decline, a hallmark of cardiomyopathy, by measuring ejection fraction (EF) and fractional shortening (FS) (Figure 2A and videos S1 and S2).

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) found that two rragca knockout zebrafish alleles obtained as byproducts of the knock-in approach produced no noticeable phenotype in homozygotes until at least 1 year of age, with unchanged cardiac pump function, indicating that rragc knock-in but not rragca knockout recapitulated cardiomyopathy and supporting a gain-of-function mechanism; they suggested the lack of knockout phenotype might reflect compensation from rragd.
quotes: Homozygous mutants for either allele did not exhibit any noticeable phenotypes until at least 1 year of age (data not shown). For example, cardiac pump function in the M1 allele remained unchanged (Figure S3C).
We did not observe any cardiac phenotypes in rragca KO fish, probably because of the compensation from rragd.

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) showed that adenoviral overexpression of RagCS75Y in neonatal rat ventricle cardiomyocytes increased cell size by 1.5-fold and elevated Nppa, Nppb, and Mhc7 with downregulated Mhc6, whereas wild-type RagC had no effect on cell size; S75Y cells showed hyperactive mTORC1 signaling (increased P-p70S6K and P-S6), cytosolic retention of TFEB with reduced TFEB target gene expression, impaired autophagy flux, accumulation of ubiquitin-conjugated proteins, and increased aggresomes.
quotes: We found that overexpression of RagCS75Y via adenovirus infection for 48 h significantly increased the cell size (by 1.5 fold) when compared to control cells infected with Ad:GFP. By contrast, overexpression of wild type RagC did not affect cell size (Figure 3A–C).

Consistent with the GOF hypothesis of the S75Y variant, we found hyperactive mTORC1 signaling as indicated by significantly higher phosphorylation levels of p70S6 kinase (P-p70S6K) and ribosomal protein S6 (P-S6) in S75Y-overexpressed NRVCMs when compared to GFP-infected control cells (Figure 4A,B).

Consistently, we noted accumulation of ubiquitin-conjugated proteins in the S75Y cell lysates, especially in the insoluble fraction that is subject to autophagic degradation (Figure 4F), as well as more aggresomes (Figure 4G).

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) found that rragc S56Y knock-in zebrafish hearts showed downregulated TFEB-controlled lysosomal genes, severely reduced LC3-II unresponsive to bafilomycin A1, elevated ubiquitin-conjugated proteins in total and insoluble fractions, and a significant increase in glycogen deposits by Periodic Acid–Schiff staining at 1 year of age, indicating dysregulated autophagy–lysosomal clearance and glycogen deposition.
quotes: Similar to the cell culture studies, transcript levels of several TFEB-controlled lysosome genes were downregulated in the rragc KI fish hearts (Figure 5A), suggesting a reduced TFEB activity.

we performed Periodic Acid–Schiff staining and observed a significant increase of glycogen deposits in rragc KI fish heart at 1 year of age (Figure 5D). Collectively, our data indicated that the RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy is characterized with dysregulated autophagy–lysosomal clearance and glycogen deposition.

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) showed by co-immunoprecipitation in AD293 cells that RagCS75Y bound TFEB with greater affinity than wild-type RagC, and that rapamycin, although it attenuated TFEB phosphorylation at S211, neither disrupted the Rags–TFEB interaction nor promoted TFEB nuclear translocation; they proposed that mTOR-independent binding between RagCS75Y and TFEB renders mTOR inhibition ineffective.
quotes: Co-immunoprecipitation assay in AD293 cells revealed a greater binding affinity between RagCS75Y and TFEB than RagCWT and TFEB (Figure 6I). Importantly, rapamycin did not attenuate Rags–TFEB interaction, nor did promote TFEB nuclear translocation (Figure 6H,I). Thus, we propose that mTOR-independent binding between RagCS75Y and TFEB renders mTOR inhibition ineffective.

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) found that mTOR inhibition with rapamycin or torin failed to normalize the enlarged size of RagCS75Y cardiomyocytes despite inhibiting mTORC1 activity, and that mtor haploinsufficiency failed to rescue cardiac pump dysfunction, cardiomyopathy marker expression, impaired growth, or reduced survival in rragc knock-in zebrafish.
quotes: Surprisingly, we found 24-hour treatment with mTOR inhibitors, including rapamycin and torin, failed to normalize the enlarged cell size in S75Y NRVCMs, despite drastic inhibition of mTORC1 activity as indicated by P-S6 expression (Figure 6A–C and Figure S4A).

Similarly, haploinsufficiency of mtor failed to exert therapeutic effect on the rragc KI model, as indicated by persistent cardiac pump dysfunction, unchanged cardiomyopathy marker expression, impaired growth, and reduced survival in double mutants (Figure 6D–F and Figure S4B).

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) found that ectopic TFEB expression normalized the cell size of RagCS75Y neonatal rat ventricle cardiomyocytes and restored autophagy flux, and that a cardiomyocyte-specific Tg(cmlc2:tfeb-GFP) transgene restored ejection fraction, fractional shortening, and vmhc expression and significantly improved survival of rragc knock-in zebrafish, suggesting that TFEB activation, but not mTOR inhibition, is a therapeutic strategy for RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy.
quotes: Indeed, the transgene was sufficient to attenuate cardiomyopathy phenotypes in the rragc KI model, as indicated by restoration of EF, FS, and vmhc expression in rragc KI;Tg(tfeb) fish compared to age matched rragc KI alone at 7 months (Figure 7D,E). The overall survival of rragc KI;Tg(tfeb) fish was significantly improved compared to rragc KI mutants (Figure 7F)
In summary, we concluded that TFEB activation, but not mTOR inhibition, is therapeutic to RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy.

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) reviewed that RagC forms heterodimeric Rag complexes with RagA or RagB whose activity depends on GDP/GTP binding status, that the Rags localize at the lysosomal surface to recruit mTORC1 and TFEB in response to amino acid availability, and that the S75 residue in RagC is evolutionarily conserved from yeast to human and lies in the phosphate-binding loop (P-loop) motif mediating GTP/GDP binding.
quotes: The Rags are localized at the surface of lysosomes to regulate cellular metabolism in response to amino acid availability. When nutrient is abundant, Rags are activated and bind to the Raptor subunit of mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) to recruit mTORC1 to the lysosome.
The S75 site in RagC is evolutionarily conserved from yeast to human beings, and is located in the phosphate-binding loop (P-loop) motif that is known to mediate GTP/GDP binding.

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) noted that many cases of RRAGC S75 mutation, including S75C, S75N, and S75F, had been identified in follicular lymphoma patients, where recurrent somatic RRAGC missense mutations clustering around the nucleotide-binding domain occurred in 17% of patients and resulted in greater GDP binding affinity and hyperactive mTORC1 signaling; in silico protein modeling predicted that S75Y likewise increases the GDP-bound state, supporting a gain-of-function mechanism.
quotes: Many cases of RRAGC S75 mutation, including S75C, S75N, S75F, were identified from follicular lymphoma patients. These mutations resulted in greater GDP binding affinity and hyperactive mTORC1 signaling, suggesting a pivotal function of RRAGC S75 in activating Rags.
Recurrent somatic mutations in RRAGC were noted in 17% patients with follicular lymphoma.

Based on in silico protein modeling via computational structural analysis, it is predicted that the S75Y mutation increases the GDP-bound state, leading to the hypothesis that S75Y is also a gain-of-function (GOF) mutation.

notes.statement: Kim et al. (2021) concluded from their in vivo and in vitro studies that S75Y is a pathogenic gain-of-function mutation in RagC that leads to cardiomyopathy, with a primary pathological step consisting of defective mTOR-TFEB signaling, and noted that it remained to be determined whether follicular lymphoma occurs in RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy patients.
quotes: These findings suggest that S75Y is a pathogenic gain-of-function mutation in RagC that leads to cardiomyopathy. A primary pathological step of RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy is defective mTOR-TFEB signaling, which can be corrected by TFEB overexpression, but not mTOR inhibition.

It remains to be determined whether follicular lymphoma occurs in RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy patients, and if so, whether and why cardiomyocytes and lymphocytes are more susceptible than the other organs to pathological damages incurred by RagC GOF.

notes.statement: Long et al. (2016) found that AD293 cells overexpressing RagC S75Y showed increased phosphorylation of S6K and S6 after amino acid deprivation compared with wild-type RagC. This indicated that the mutation made cells partly insensitive to amino acid deprivation and activated mTORC1 signaling.
quotes: By contrast, S6K and S6 phosphorylation levels were increased in cells transfected with RagCS75Y (Figure 3A, B), indicating that the S75Y mutation rendered cells partially insensitive to amino acid deprivation and resulted in activated mTORC1 signaling.

notes.statement: Long et al. (2016) used in silico modeling and molecular dynamics simulation of RagC S75Y. They predicted that the mutant could not coordinate Mg2+, would disrupt ligand interactions, and would expand the GDP-bound conformation, similar to the engineered GDP-bound mutant S75L.
quotes: The S75 sidechain coordinated with Mg2+ (Figure 2A and 2D), but both S75Y and S75L introduced hydrophobic residues which were unable to coordinate Mg2+
MD trajectories were summarized using RMSD and revealed consistent conformational expansion of the GDP-bound state for both S75Y and S75L (Figure 2G-H).

notes.statement: Long et al. (2016) noted that the S75Y mutation lay in the highly conserved P-loop (G1) of the GTPase domain and was absent from ExAC. ExAC controls carried no missense or truncating variants in the RRAGC GTPase binding domain. The authors could not exclude synergistic heterozygosity involving other candidate variants.
quotes: The de novo missense mutation occurred in the highly conserved GTPase binding-domain (Figure 1D) and was absent in the ExAc database. Further, there was complete absence of missense and truncating variants in the GTPase binding-domain of RRAGC among ExAC controls.
While synergistic heterozygosity involving one or more of the identified candidate variants cannot be excluded as contributing to the disease phenotype
